mutations.survived_summary: M6 (show_world adds a 'free_unlocks' fallback): 1/13 my mutations SURVIVED. The test_panel has no positive control that asserts the codex reads ONLY consequence.archive.unlocked; a fallback/merge that also reads another key would not be caught. This is a coverage gap, not an open unlock path (Q3's structural answer still holds: there is no public method that adds to _unlocked). Suggested test: a world with 'free_unlocks: ["archive.bubble"]' but no 'consequence.archive.unlocked' should NOT unlock archive.bubble.

findings.issue: Coverage gap: the codex's locked-entry gate is well-tested for the canonical world shape (consequence.archive.unlocked). It is not tested for worlds that include a SECOND key like 'free_unlocks' or 'story_unlocks': a fallback that also reads such a key would pass test_panel. Mutation M6 (show_world reads 'free_unlocks' first, falls back) SURVIVED.
findings.suggestion: Add a single positive control in test_panel: show_world({'free_unlocks': ['archive.bubble']}) expects 0 disabled rows; show_world({}) after that still expects 0. The existing 'a world without the archive section locks everything' test (line 134) gives the negative direction; the missing case is 'a world with a different unlock key also locks everything'.

non_blocking_observations: The M4.7 fix from iter 16 (commit 3939912) added 'env -u AI_LIVE' to the two Makefile lore-test run lines (rule A of ai-live-guard). The RED was 'make ai-live-guard' naming Makefile:724 and :725; the GREEN is confirmed in iter 16 and in this evaluation (the lines now use env -u AI_LIVE).

The 'no public method to unlock an entry' test is structural (string match on method names). It is brittle: renaming show_world to showWorld, or adding a private helper named _unlock_*, would silently break the test while still being correct (or correct while still being wrong). A semantic test (lock rows: any world without the canonical archive.unlocked key keeps them all disabled) is more robust.
